Replay

Every screen the player faced, in order. Arrow keys step, space plays; the line underneath is the keys it sent and why.

(no screens were recorded)

What it would do differently

The leads the player wrote, each with where it happened and what would settle it. An ask is a link into the replay above.

  1. A depth-2 crow can kill a CL1 Gnome Mage in one turn, and it never sleeps.

    Evidence: the crow's row in lib/gamedata/monster.txt — speed:120, sleepiness:0, blow:BITE:HURT:1d3 twice — and the death screen (HP -2/8).

    How to test it: one run that walks onto depth 2 and deliberately finds a crow, with the hit points and the number of crow turns it took, and one that does the same against a wild cat (also sleepiness:0, AC 14, speed 120, two claw/bite blows) to see whether the two are equally bad, and against a white harpy (speed 110, sleepiness:10) to see whether a sleeping monster is worth anything.

  2. The spell list's rows are the learned spells; the screen prints the whole book.

    Evidence: the list at ask 162 printed seven rows with unknown and difficult beside them, but pressing b and then 2 and Enter cast Find Traps (row 2) again and again, and the header said cursor at 15,4 — the fourth screen row, which is Find Traps.

    How to test it: one run that studies a second spell at CL2 and casts it, which also tests whether the +4 experience of a first cast of a studied spell really is paid (the source says player_exp_gain(player, e * spell->slevel) on the first working cast, src/player-spell.c:527).

    ask 162 · turn 5,742

  3. The first use of an unknown potion is worth its kind's level, and at depth 1 the pool's best kind is worth five.

    Evidence: the Yellow Potion was a Potion of Neutralize Poison (level:5 in object.txt) and paid 5 experience in one ask (NXT 8 → 3).

    How to test it: a run that drinks every unknown potion it finds, on a fresh level, and reports the kinds it drew against the pool's weights (Neutralize Poison 60, Speed 40, Heroism 40, Boldness 40, Cure Light Wounds 80, and the bad five at 10 each).

  4. A rest is one decision for two spell points, and a rest is the only way to make a spell affordable.

    Evidence: R, backspace, *, Enter on the down staircase at ask 182 filled the bar 0/2 → 2/2 and was not interrupted, while the spell points regenerate at about one per 71 actions while walking (player_regen_mana(): msp × 197 + 524 in 65536ths per action).

    How to test it: one run that measures the rest's length in game turns on a swept corridor against one beside a sleeping monster, because the interruption cost is what decides where a mage can rest.

    ask 182 · turn 6,284

  5. The detection spell is the only way to find the rooms of a level, and the rooms are where the monsters are.

    Evidence: the Find Traps cast on depth 2 found seven doors and the down staircase in two asks; the room on depth 1 held two monsters and the corridors I walked held none.

    How to test it: a run that counts monsters per room visited against monsters per corridor tile swept, with the doors marked from a cast, and which reports whether the doors the spell finds are the room entrances or mostly closets — on the level I died on, one of the four doors had no floor on the far side at all.

  6. A level's known area can be a dead-end tree, and then the only way on is a fresh level.

    Evidence: on depth 1 every known tile led back to the room I started in; the way out was a one-tile notch in its east wall and then 23 tiles of dark.

    How to test it: one run that, at the start of a level, counts the known doorways and asks whether any of them leads to ground the character has not seen — the answer decides whether to spend the level's budget on walking or on rerolling it.

What it kept

- First note, mmf-mage (seed 1, Gnome Mage, build g9afcd64-dirty). Files I actually opened before my first keypress: PLAYGAME.txt, AGENTS.md, docs/BRIEF.md, manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md (all 551 lines, incl. my class block in section 9), agents/minimax/COMMON.md and agents/minimax/MAGE.md. My own playbook (minimax COMMON.md + MAGE.md) is among them, and I will follow its playbook --check later. I wrote no tools of my own; I will use the shared tools/screen ones (look.py, explore.py, map.py) as they are. Plan from my own pages: shop before descending (oil, one Cure Light Wounds, one Phase Door, armour), then Find Traps/Doors/Stairs ONCE per fresh level, then l>g to the staircase it finds, and press M every few asks -- the M map shows remembered staircases I have walked past. (ask 1)
- DECISION (ask 14): studied Find Traps, Doors & Stairs, NOT Magic Missile, contrary to my own MAGE.md 2 correction ('Magic Missile first'). Reason, mine: at CL1 the whole level-1 exp economy is the bottleneck -- CL2 needs 12 exp (Gnome 120%), the best depth-1 kill is a small kobold at 5 exp, and kobolds are AC 24, which my thrown oil (to-hit 11) can only hit on the 12% floor. Depth 2 pays double for the same kill, so one cast + one walk to the staircase it reveals moves the whole hunt to where the exp is. Magic Missile is available at CL2 (2nd slot: num_allowed = adj_mag_study x lev / 100, so CL2 allows 2), when SP also doubles (4 SP, one point per 50 actions). Evidence: class.txt mage spell list (Magic Missile L1 1sp exp 4; Find Traps L1 1sp exp 2), monster.txt (small kobold 8hp AC24 exp5 at depth1; blubbering icky thing 18hp AC4 exp8 at depth2 = 16 exp at CL1 = CL2 in one kill); hit_chance formula 12% floor. (ask 14)
- TOWN NAVIGATION (ask 16): the aim.py recipe (* + digits + g) FAILED in the town: * opens the Target mode with the cursor on my own square, and my square was the down staircase (INTERESTING, terrain.txt flags STAIR|DOWNSTAIR|INTERESTING), so the first digit printed the description and the NEXT digit aborted the mode ('Target Aborted'), after which the rest of the string was run as raw movement and I walked 2 tiles south by accident. Source: ui-target.c target_set_interactive -> target_set_interactive_aux -> aux_terrain consumes a key whenever the cursor square is interesting, and returns true (stop) for any key that is not Enter or space. Also terrain.txt: SHOP tiles carry INTERESTING too, so aiming AT a store digit cannot work either. In the town I use plain digit walking over the drawn map instead (map.py --to gives the route); the routes it printed were checked step by step against the panel and none crosses rubble. (ask 16)
- ARMOUR DECISION (ask 20): this Armoury has no Soft Leather Armour, no shield and no helm, so my MAGE.md shopping list does not exist in this seed; what it has is Studded Leather Armour 150 (AC12, 10 lb, to-hit -1), Robe 36 (AC2), Gauntlets 24 (AC3), Iron Shod Boots 84 (AC4), Leather Gloves 6 (AC1). I bought Studded+Robe+Gauntlets = AC 17 for 210 of 256 gold. The Studded's (-1) is a real cost and I checked it in the source: calc_bonuses (player-calcs.c) does state->to_h += obj->to_h for every worn item that is not a weapon or a bow, and chance_of_missile_hit_base (player-attack.c:134) adds p->state.to_h to the throw to-hit for a THROWING item -- and a Flask of oil carries the THROWING flag (object.txt). So the armour costs my thrown oil one point of to-hit (11 -> 10), which is ~7 points of hit rate against an AC-14 target (12+83*(11-9)/11 = 27% -> 12+83*(10-9)/10 = 20%). I judged +7 AC worth more: a depth-2 soldier with to-hit 15 hits me 12+83*(15-9)/15 = 51% of the time at AC 10 and 12+83*(15-11)/15 = 33% at AC 17. (ask 20)
- STORE RENUMBERING, MEASURED (ask 21): buying the last Studded Leather Armour REMOVED its row, so every letter below it moved up by one -- Leather Scale Mail took 'f', the Gauntlets went from 'm' to 'j', and the Iron Shod Boots took 'm'. My queued 'pm1\ny' therefore opened the Boots' sub-menu instead of buying Gauntlets, and the store shows '(Enter to select, ESC) Command for 4 Pairs of Iron Shod Boots'. Gold moved 256 -> 70, so the Studded (150) and the Robe (36) were bought and nothing else. The rule in my COMMON.md is right and the fix is to buy the LAST row first: every earlier letter then stays valid. (ask 21)
- ROUTE TOOL WARNING (ask 24): the shared map.py route for the Alchemist (7111141477777441774441741) uses a diagonal step from (33,15) to (32,14) whose two orthogonal neighbours are BOTH rubble, so the game would refuse that diagonal and the digit string would stop there. I recomputed an orthogonal-only route over the same panel: 8444444444444444448444444442, 28 steps, every step on a drawn floor tile, ending on the store digit. Rule for me: in the town, check the corners of every diagonal step before sending it. (ask 24)
- STORE BUYS ARE NOT WORN (ask 27): do_cmd_buy (store.c:1650) only copies the object into the pack and charges the gold; there is no wear prompt in ui-store.c, so armour bought in a shop has to be worn by hand with 'w'. I checked the source rather than assuming. (ask 27)
- ARMOUR SLOTS (ask 28): the wear prompt shows the four bought pieces as g) 2 Wooden Torches, i) a Robe, m) Studded Leather Armour, n) Leather Gloves, o) Gauntlets -- the letters are the PACK letters (Inven: g-o), and non-wearable pack items keep their letters between them. The Robe and the Studded Leather Armour are both type 'soft armor', so they share the BODY slot: only one can be worn, so the Robe (AC 2) is dead money against the Studded (AC 12) and I wear only the Studded. Expected AC = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16, not 18. Also measured: wearing an item takes it out of the pack and re-letters everything after it, so wearing from the LAST letter backwards keeps every earlier letter valid -- the same trick as buying the last store row first. (ask 28)

- THE MACHINE RESTARTED (ask 40): the host rebooted while I was playing and the game process died with it (the runner reported 'no new question within 60s'; the run was 'stopped, saved'). The documented way on is borg_runner carry-on, which REPLAYS the old keys into a fresh process: the new run is runs/mmf-mage.2, it printed identical: true (the replay reproduced my game exactly), and it left the game waiting at ask 40, turn 1131 with my notebook inherited. So the two runs are one character and one line of play; the name changed only because the process had to change. The replay also executed the '.6' I had queued when the machine died: the run east carried me 4 tiles and stopped at a quartz vein. (ask 40)
- UNKNOWN POTION, IDENTIFIED AS A POTION NOT A FLASK (ask 41): ']' says 'a Purple Speckled Potion, 7 N 1 E'. The flavour name does NOT name the kind -- lib/gamedata/flavor.txt lists 'Purple Speckled' as flavour 232, one of many random ones -- so it is an unknown kind. I recomputed the depth-1 potion pool from object.txt's alloc bands: Cure Light Wounds 80, Neutralize Poison 60, Speed 40, Heroism 40, Boldness 40, Slime Mold Juice 10, against Sleep 10, Blindness 10, Confusion 10, Poison 10, Slowness 10 -- so 270/320 good (84%) and 50/320 bad (16%). The first use pays (kind level + my level/2)/my level, so at CL1 it pays the kind's own level: expected about 1.5 experience, which is a tenth of what CL2 costs. I am CARRYING it, not drinking it: at full hit points the good outcomes (heals, heroism) mostly do nothing, while the bad tail includes Poison (object.txt: level 3, effect TIMED_INC:POISONED) and Sleep (TIMED_INC:PARALYZED), which are lethal to an 8-hit-point mage. I will drink it when I am safe, or when I need it. (ask 41)
- A KEY WENT MISSING MID-WALK (ask 42): I sent '88888886' (7 north, then 1 east) from (57,7) and expected to land on the potion at (58,0); the walk put me at (58,1), one tile short, and the potion was still on the floor. Exactly one key of the eight was lost: the message line was empty, no condition changed (no confusion), my hit points were unchanged, and the turn counter shows the steps I did make. The mushroom patch on the other side of the corridor is the only thing near enough to have disturbed me, and the game flushes the input queue on a disturbance (src/cmd-cave.c disturb()), which would swallow the rest of the string. Whatever the cause, the count of keys is not the count of steps: I now check where I actually am with look.py after every multi-key walk. (ask 42)
- THE FIRST CAST FAILED, SILENTLY (asks 34-45): the character sheet shows Cur Exp 0, and Find Traps pays 2 experience on its first successful cast (class.txt: spell:Find Traps, Doors & Stairs:1:1:20:2 -- the last field is the experience, and player-spell.c pays e * spell->slevel on the first success). So the cast at ask 34 failed its 12% roll, which also means the spell never ran its effect and the level was never marked with SQUARE_DTRAP -- the level is still CLEAN, so a cast now will be the first real one. The failed cast printed NO message either: screen-35's message line is empty, while player-spell.c prints 'You failed to concentrate hard enough!' on a failure. I cannot explain the missing message from the screen; maybe the trailing space in 'c ' was eaten by the input flush that the same failure triggers (event_signal(EVENT_INPUT_FLUSH)), or the message was overwritten. This time I sent 'mc' with no trailing space so I can see. (ask 45)
- THE CHARACTER SHEET IS A MENU THAT EATS KEYS (ask 46): after 'C' the sheet stays up ('c' to change name, 'f' to file, 'h' to change mode, or ESC), so my 'mc' meant 'change name' and opened the rename prompt instead of opening the spell list. Two escapes are needed to get back: one for the prompt, one for the sheet. This is the same rule as my COMMON.md's 'to leave two menus, send \e\e, not \ee' -- the letter e is not the escape. (ask 46)
- THE SPELL WORKS, AND ITS MESSAGES COME ON A -more- (ask 49): 'You sense no traps. You sense the presence of doors!' -- so the first cast that really ran found doors this time and no traps. The message ends in -more-, so the stair message (the third effect, DETECT_STAIRS) is on the next page: the effects run in the order the class lists them, DETECT_TRAPS then DETECT_DOORS then DETECT_STAIRS, and only the first two fit on the page. This also explains the empty message line of the first cast: a failed cast prints 'You failed to concentrate hard enough!' and the input flush that goes with it (player-spell.c) can swallow the rest of the key string. (ask 49)
- THE SPELL FOUND TWO DOWN STAIRCASES (ask 50): the whole-level M map now draws a '>' at box (42,0) and another at box (60,6), with my '@' at box (45,8) and the up staircase '<' at box (33,14). The M map is the whole 198x66 level scaled to 78x22 boxes (display_map in ui-map.c computes row = y * map_hgt / cave->height), so 1 box is about 2.5 tiles: the near staircase is about 8 tiles west and 20 tiles north, the other about 38 tiles east. Both are now KNOWN, so l>g can walk to one. This is minimaxflash-2.2's measurement holding: on a level the detection spell has not already broken, one cast plus one walk is the whole staircase hunt. (ask 50)
- STAIRCASE HUNT, THE SECOND TIME (asks 47-52): the second cast worked and the M map showed TWO down staircases, at box (42,0) and box (60,6). 'l>g' then walked me 7 tiles and stopped at an open door, 3 tiles short; a second 'l>g' covered the last 3 and I am standing on the down staircase (the status line says 'DTrap Down staircase'). Two asks for the walk, and the status line now carries 'DTrap', which is the spell's SQUARE_DTRAP marking showing up in the conditions. So the whole hunt from a clean level was: 1 cast + 1 M + 2 walks = 4 asks, plus the walk's first attempt stopping short. minimaxflash-2.2's 'one cast and one walk' was close; the extra walk was needed because the first one stopped at a door. (ask 52)
- WHY I LEFT DEPTH 2 WITHOUT A FIGHT (asks 53-55): the chamber I arrived in holds three cave spiders (7 hp, AC 19, 1d4, SPEED 120 so two blows a turn) -- the manual's swarm of 2d8 -- all asleep, one blue yeek (7 hp, AC 16, 1d5, sleepiness 10) asleep, a gold pile, and a mushroom patch. My arithmetic says the yeek is one wake-event from waking: monster_reduce_sleep (mon-move.c) reduces a sleeping monster's sleep by 100/local_noise when the player is within about 10 tiles, and the yeek's sleep is only 10. Oil is a 12% attack against AC 16 (hit_chance: 2*AC/3 = 10 equals my to-hit 10, so I am on the flat floor), so the yeek needs about eight throws, which is about 22 damage of bites at AC 15 -- more than my 8 hit points -- and the three spiders sit next to the yeek, so hitting it wakes them (their GROUP_AI and friends:100:2d8:Same). At 8 hp and 0 spell points I was not going to open that fight. Going up costs two asks and buys a full spell bar, a safe place to try the unknown potion, and a fresh level. (ask 54)
- THE MONSTER LISTING LEAVES A PROMPT (ask 55): '[' prints the monster list and then '(Press any key to continue.)', and that prompt eats the next key -- my '<' was consumed by it and the game did not move (the turn counter did not change). So after '[' I must send a harmless key first, and the up staircase came one ask later than I planned. (ask 55)
- THE REST PROMPT (ask 56): the field is pre-filled with '& ', so 'R' + '*' + Enter would rest only 'as needed'. The one-ask full rest is R + BACKSPACE + '*' + Enter: the first backspace deletes the whole field (src/ui-input.c 'if this is the first time round, backspace means delete all'). I am resting ON the down staircase of a fresh depth 1, so if anything comes, one '<' takes me back to the town. At 8 hit points with 0 spell points, a full bar is worth an ask. (ask 56)
- THE TRAILING NEWLINE BYTE IS DROPPED, THE TWO-CHARACTER ESCAPE IS NOT (ask 57): I sent R + backspace + '*' + a real newline byte (printf '\n'), the field was cleared and '*' typed, but the Enter never arrived -- the screen still showed the rest prompt. The frontend drops a trailing LF byte because that is the one a text editor adds (patch/src/main-agent.c), so the Enter has to be sent as the two characters backslash-n, which the runner turns into KC_ENTER. My COMMON.md says exactly this and I still wrote it the wrong way once. (ask 57)
- REST WORKS, AND THE SPELL BAR IS THE REAL CURRENCY (ask 58): one full rest on the down staircase took 610 game turns (61 player actions) and filled the bar from 0/2 to 2/2 -- that is 0.028 spell points an action while resting, so 71 actions for a point when awake and about 36 while resting. Resting is ONE ask, so spell points are cheap in asks and expensive in turns: what they cost is the turns you spend standing still while a level's monsters wake up. This run's whole budget should be read in that currency: a cast is worth about 70 actions of walking, and a mage's kills on depth 1 pay 1 to 5 experience each while depth 2 pays 2 to 16. (ask 58)
- THE ']' GLYPH IS BOOTS, NOT A HELM (ask 70): the item on the floor was 'a Pair of Leather Sandals [1,+0]' -- in object.txt the ']' graphics belong to the boots (Pair of Iron Shod Boots graphics:]:U) and the helms use ']' too but with a different colour, so a text screen cannot tell them apart. I read the glyph as a helm and it was a pair of sandals: +1 AC, 2 lb. The lesson for me: look at the object before assuming what the glyph means -- 'l' + a direction describes the square, and the message when you pick it up names the kind. (ask 70)
- MONSTERS ARE PLACED AWAY FROM THE START (asks 66-73): I ran 30 tiles along the big hall on depth 2 and met nothing, and the reason is in the generator rather than in my luck: classic_gen places monsters away from the up staircase, so the first corridor and the first hall are empty. That is also why the Find Traps spell matters more than my own eyes here -- the spell finds the staircase, and the staircase is where the monsters are. I have spent 20 asks exploring an empty level; the cast costs 2 asks and points at the part of the level that has anything in it. (ask 72)
- DEPTH 3 TARGETS, FROM THE DATA (ask 76): I read monster.txt for depth 3 and the good targets for a CL1 mage with thrown oil (to-hit 10) are the metallic blue centipede (12 hp, AC 7, experience 7, so 21 experience on depth 3 at CL1, and it hits for 1d2+1d2), the metallic red centipede (18 hp, AC 10, experience 12, so 36) and the yellow worm mass (18 hp, AC 4, experience 4). The bad ones are the black naga (AC 60, 1d8 -- oil cannot touch it at all), the radiation eye (GAZE:LOSE_STR), the silver jelly (TOUCH:EAT_LIGHT takes my torch), the spotted mushroom patch (SPORE:POISON:2d4) and Sméagol (invisible, steals gold). One centipede is CL2 with 11 experience to spare, so depth 3 is where the exp is. (ask 76)
- HOW MANY MONSTERS A LEVEL HAS, AND WHERE (ask 80, from the source): classic_gen places i = z_info->level_monster_min + randint1(8) + k monsters, k = MAX(MIN(depth/3,10),2), with pick_and_place_distant_monster(c, p->grid, 0, true, depth) -- so they are placed at any distance from the up staircase (the 'distant' in the name means only 'not on the start square'), and they start ASLEEP. That is the correction to my earlier note: on a classic level the monsters are NOT kept away from the up staircase, they are simply sparse -- about fifty of them on 198x66 squares, one per 250. A corridor of ten tiles therefore holds a monster about four per cent of the time, and a 10x10 room about a third. So a room is worth ten corridors, and the Find Traps spell is worth a lot more than the staircase: it reveals the DOORS, which is a map of where the rooms are. (ask 80)
- DECISION: THE TOWN TRIP (ask 83). What I have learned by now: exploration on a 'classic' level is slow (a run stops at every junction, so a run is 1 to 12 tiles and an aimed walk with an unknown destination gives a bogus one-tile path), the monsters are sparse (about fifty on 198x66) and they start asleep, and my spell bar is empty at 0/2 after two casts. One spell point costs about 71 actions of walking (0.014 per action), so a cast is 6 to 20 asks of running -- while the town is two '<' away and a full rest there is safe. So: go up, rest, buy a second heal and a second escape with the 55 gold, then descend with 2 spell points, one cast per level for the staircase hunt. The alternative was to keep hunting for a kill with an empty bar and 8 hit points, and that is the plan that gets a mage killed. (ask 83)
- STAIRCASE PAIRING, MEASURED (asks 84-86): '<' (ascend) only works from an UP staircase and lands me on a DOWN staircase of the level above, and '>' (descend) only from a DOWN staircase. I walked to depth 3's up staircase, pressed '<' and arrived on depth 2's DOWN staircase; pressing '<' again did nothing at all (the turn counter did not move), which is why two '<' presses left me exactly where I was. The pairs are: town's down <-> depth 1's up, depth 1's down <-> depth 2's up, depth 2's down <-> depth 3's up. So the way UP from depth 2 is to find depth 2's UP staircase, and from there I arrive on depth 1's DOWN staircase, which needs a SECOND up staircase to reach the town. Two casts, and I have one spell point. The Scroll of Word of Recall in my pack is the cheap way: read it in the dungeon and it takes me to the town, for the price of its 15 to 34 player-turn timer. (ask 86)
- WORD OF RECALL, USED AS A WAY HOME (ask 87): the read prompt lists my scrolls as f) a Scroll of Phase Door and g) a Scroll of Word of Recall -- so the pack letters are not in the order I assumed (the Phase Door I bought in town is 'f', the Recall 'g'). Reading it starts the 15 to 34 player-action timer (src/game-world.c decrements the counter once every ten game turns). I will KEEP WALKING while it runs -- minimaxflash-3 read a Recall and stood still for forty turns and a cave spider killed it at 26 of 43 hit points, so standing still is how that run died. (ask 87)
- THE RECALL TIMER, MEASURED (asks 89-91): the timer is 15 to 34 PLAYER actions (src/game-world.c decrements it once every ten game turns), and a run in this level is only one to four actions because it stops at every junction -- so walking it out would have cost 10 to 30 asks. A rest is 61 actions in ONE ask, so I am resting and letting the timer fire during it. The rest is interrupted if a monster reaches me, and I have two answers for that: a Scroll of Phase Door and a Potion of Cure Light Wounds. That is a much better risk than 20 asks of walking. (ask 91)
- THE SHOPS RESTOCK, AND THE HELM IS GONE (ask 94): the Armoury today has no helm at all -- Robes, a Robe of Resist Fire, Leather Scale Mail (750), Leather Gloves, Gauntlets and Iron Shod Boots (84) -- where yesterday it had the Studded Leather Armour I am wearing. store_update runs once a game day and shuffles the stock on a 1-in-store_shuffle chance, so a shopping list written on one day is not a shopping list on the next. The Manual Cap I was going to buy for 24 gold does not exist today, so the 60 gold goes to what does: a Cloak (6, +1 AC, the cloak slot is empty), four flasks of oil (12, and my burden has 13.8 lb of room), a Potion of Cure Light Wounds (20) and a Scroll of Phase Door (15). (ask 94)

The trailing 'y' that I meant as a confirmation is exactly what opened the Blessing row. (ask 101)

My first 's' came straight after the Escape that closed the Blessing command prompt and was eaten by it -- two menus need two escapes, which is the rule my COMMON.md already states. This time the sell prompt should open. (ask 102)

The working sequence is 'ma' in one ask (the book prompt and the book) and then 'c' in the next ask for the spell: the spell list takes a key of its own to answer, so the third key of 'mac' is consumed by the list appearing and the cast needs one more key than I thought. The list's letters are the book's spells, not the spells I know: it shows all seven with 'unknown' for the ones I have not learned. (ask 113)
- THE AIMED AND LOOK-MODE WALKS ARE SHORT WHEN THE GROUND BETWEEN IS UNKNOWN (ask 116): 'l>g' moved one tile and stopped, although the staircase the spell found is known. The reason is in find_path (player-path.c): only_known = square_isknown(start) AND square_isknown(dest), so with a known destination but unknown ground in between the path is computed over remembered ground only and comes out short or empty. The M map knows where the staircase is (two of them, at box 9,7 and box 26,4, against my box 13,12) but the panel does not show it, so the route has to be walked in pieces. The look-mode trick is the piece that works: a direction key in look mode jumps the cursor to the NEXT INTERESTING SQUARE and the message line names it with its exact offset, which is also how I learn how far the staircase is. (ask 116)
- THE WALK IS SHORT BECAUSE THE GROUND BETWEEN IS NOT KNOWN (ask 117): on a fresh level only the square I stand on, the squares the detection spell memorised (the doors and the stairs) and the few tiles my torch lights are known. find_path's only_known test needs BOTH ends known and a path over remembered ground, and there is none between me and a staircase 15 tiles north, so the walk is one tile. The piece that works is plain digit walking: a digit string stops only at a WALL, not at a turn, so eight '8's in one ask cover eight tiles of corridor if the corridor runs straight, and the message line says how far it got. (ask 117)
- WHERE THE STAIRCASE IS, FROM THE M MAP (ask 118): the M map's boxes are 2.5 tiles wide and 3 tiles high (78 boxes for 198 tiles, 22 for 66), my '@' is at box (14,12), so I stand at level (35,36) and the level's down staircases are at level (23,21) and (66,12) -- twelve west and fifteen north of me, and thirty east and twenty-four north. The nearer one is four rows above the top of my panel, and the corridor north of my square is a wall, so the way there is a loop: south, west, then north. And the walking has to be done with digit strings, because the pathfinder's path is computed over remembered ground and a fresh level has almost none. (ask 118)
- THE MONSTER DENSITY, MEASURED (asks 116-122): the level has z_info->level_monster_min + randint1(8) + k monsters, about fifty, on 13,068 squares -- one per 250. My torch shows a 3x3 patch, so to sweep the level I would have to walk about 260 squares, and my best walking rate is about eight tiles an ask, so a search for one kill is thirty asks. That is the real bottleneck of this run, and it is not the fighting: the fighting is cheap (a flask of oil is 9 to 36 damage and a giant green frog on depth 2 dies to one or two), the FINDING is expensive. The Find Traps spell is worth more for its doors than for its stairs, because a door is a map of where the rooms are, and a room is a hundred squares of concentrated search. (ask 122)

So a run walks to the EDGE OF THE KNOWN MAP and no further: mine stopped after one tile at (34,13) because (33,14),(34,14),(35,14) are unknown. The AIMED WALK ('*' then digits then 'g') is the tool for the dark, because find_path treats unknown ground as passable there. - THE FIRST-CAST EXPERIENCE, FROM THE SOURCE (ask 161): player-spell.c line 527-533 pays 'e * spell->slevel' the first time a spell WORKS, where e is the last field of the class.txt spell line: Find Traps 2 x 1 = 2, Light Room 4 x 1 = 4, Magic Missile 4 x 1 = 4. So a first cast of Light Room is worth 4 experience - a third of the 12 a Gnome needs for CL2 - and it also lights every square within two grids and, because I am in a room, the WHOLE ROOM, which shows me every monster standing in it. Two costs I did not know: the mana is taken whether the cast succeeds or fails (the smana block is outside the success branch), and a failure signals EVENT_INPUT_FLUSH, which is the input flush that eats the rest of a key string. Also measured: the throw sequence is Escape (to clear the monster list's 'press any key'), 'v' (throw prompt), 'a' (the flask of oil - the throw list has its own letters and oil is 'a'), '4' (that direction) - and it worked in one ask: 'Your Flask of oil hits the white worm mass.' So the class has three CL1 spells and the first cast of each pays 4, 4 and 2 experience. - THE CAST MENU IS A MENU, AND ITS LETTERS DID NOT ANSWER (ask 163-164): pressing 'b' for Light Room did nothing at all - the spell list stayed up, no mana was spent and no message appeared - even though ui-menu.c's get_cursor_key should have matched it (the menu's selections are all_letters_nohjkl and MN_CASELESS_TAGS makes 'b' and 'B' agree). The menu has another way in: the digit keys are directions (target_dir_allow takes any digit as a direction), so '2' moves the cursor down one row and Enter selects the row under it. The cursor starts on the first row, so '2' then Enter is Light Room. My own past life used 'c' for Find Traps, which is why the letter route looked certain. (ask 164) (ask 164)
- HOW THE CAST MENU REALLY WORKS (ask 163-165): the spell list is a scroll menu. Its letters do not select - pressing 'b' for Light Room only MOVED the cursor to that row and left the menu open (the menu wants a double tap), and the trailing space does nothing because all seven rows fit on one page. The digit keys are directions, so '2' moved the cursor down one row and Enter selected the row under it - which is how I cast Find Traps by accident: the cursor had been on Light Room (row 1) and my '2' took it to row 2, Find Traps. A NEW menu starts with the cursor on row 0, so Enter alone selects Magic Missile. The rule for this game: MOVE the cursor with a digit, then press Enter - never trust the letter. The cast printed 'You sense no traps. You sense no doors.' which is the third effect of a Find Traps cast (the doors were already known), and the message ends in -more-, so the next answer starts with a space. (ask 165) (ask 165)

So the +4 experience from Magic Missile is still waiting for a cast that works. The snake (large white snake, 11 hp, AC 36) is the right target for it: Magic Missile is 3d4 that never resists, so two casts are about four flasks of oil, which at 12 per cent hit rate against AC 36 is 2.7 expected damage a flask. I am NOT drinking it here: the pool is 84 per cent harmless but the bad tail includes Sleep (paralysis, and a paralysed mage next to a snake dies) and Confusion (which blocks casting for 1d4 turns and randomises every direction), and the good cases pay at most the kind's own level of experience. The message after that cast was the Find Traps message's second page ('You sense the presence of stairs!'), so the second cast printed nothing of its own, and the spell list had shown Magic Missile as 'unknown' yet selecting it took a spell point and did no damage - which is what a failed 14 per cent cast of an UNLEARNED spell looks like. In this build the cast list shows every spell in the book, with 'unknown' for the ones not learned and 'difficult' for those above my level, and the selection is not filtered: so a CL1 mage can cast Magic Missile (3d4, never resists) and Light Room out of the book without studying them, and each one's first successful cast pays 4 experience. If that is right, the 8 experience I need for CL2 is 2 x Magic Missile + 2 x Light Room, for 4 spell points. (ask 168) (ask 168)
- WHERE THE KNOWN LEVEL TOUCHES THE DARK (ask 169): I computed it from the tiles, and there are exactly TWO places: the corridor tile at panel (34,5) (which opens into the dark north of the vertical corridor) and the floor tile at (59,15), a one-tile notch in this room's east wall, which opens into the dark at (60,14). So this room is sealed but for that notch, and the notch points east and north-east - the way to the third down staircase the Find Traps cast found, at M-box (36,21) = level (91,63), which is 33 east and 9 south of where I stand. The whole known part of this level is a dead-end tree: the big room is sealed, the vertical corridor's north end is the up staircase (a dead end with three walls), the east corridor ends at this room's door, and this room's only other opening is the notch. So the way out of the known level is the notch, and everything else must be found in the dark. (ask 169) (ask 169)
- THE M MAP EATS THE NEXT KEY (ask 169-170): the whole-level map ends with 'Hit any key to continue', so my 'l>g' was swallowed and the character did not move and no message appeared - which looked exactly like the walk failing. The manual says the same of a '-more-': the first key of the next answer is eaten, so an answer after M or after a two-page message must start with a space. (ask 170) (ask 170)
- THE GREEDY WALK IS GOOD WHEN THE GROUND IS OPEN (ask 170-171): 'l>g' walked me 29 tiles in ONE ask - from the room at panel (55,15) to (26,11) - and the panel around the new position is entirely blank, so it went straight through ground nobody had seen. That is the pathfinder's fallback: path_nearest_known computes the distance with unknown squares treated as passable, so the walk follows a line into the dark and stops at the first real wall. The two known down staircases are now at different distances from me and the game picked one; the level's third staircase (level 91,63) is drawn on the panel 20 south and 20 east of my new position. (ask 171) (ask 171)
- WHERE I STAND (ask 171-172): the walk did move me - three tiles east to level (61,54), the room's east edge - and the panel scrolled 32 columns, which is what made it look like a 29-tile jump. The M map and the panel now agree: the '@' is at M-box (25,18) = level (63,54), the snake is at M-box (22,19) = level (56,57), and the level's third down staircase is at M-box (36,21) = level (91,63), 30 east and 9 south of me. The greedy 'l>g' stopped after three tiles because the wall of the room is there. (ask 172) (ask 172)
- THE PACK, AND THE VALUE OF A POTION (ask 172-174): a) Book of Magic Spells [First Spells], b) 4 Rations of Food, c) 23 Flasks of oil (46 lb), d) 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, e) 2 Yellow Potions (both '!' items were potions of the same flavour, though the kind is unknown and the two need not be the same kind), f) 2 Scrolls of Phase Door, g) 2 Wooden Torches (5000 turns), i) a Robe [2,+1], m) a Set of Leather Gloves [1,+0]. From object.txt the depth-1 potion pool and each kind's level (which is what the first use pays at CL1): Cure Light Wounds 0 (weight 80), Neutralize Poison 5 (60), Speed 1 (40), Heroism 1 (40), Boldness 1 (40), Slime Mold Juice 0 (10), Sleep 0 (10), Blindness 0 (10), Confusion 0 (10), Poison 3 (10), Slowness 1 (10). So a potion is worth 1.4 experience on average and the dangerous ones are 3 per cent each - a far better rate than a kill, which pays 1 to 3 experience for ten or twenty decisions of finding it. (ask 174) (ask 174)
- THE ITEM MENU IS BETWEEN THE PACK LETTER AND THE ACTION (ask 174-175): pressing 'q' opens 'Select Item' and the pack letter then opens the ITEM'S COMMAND MENU (I)nspect, q) Quaff, d) Drop, D) Drop All, v) Throw, {) Inscribe, k) Ignore) - so a quaff is two keys and a throw is three. The manual's line that the quaff prompt uses the pack letters is right about the letter but not about the step in between. (ask 175) (ask 175)
- THE FIRST YELLOW POTION WAS A NEUTRALIZE POISON (ask 175-176): the message reads 'You have a Potion of Neutralize Poison (e)' and the sidebar's NXT went from 8 to 3, so the first use of a kind pays that kind's own level and this one was level 5 - the best kind in the depth-1 pool, 19 per cent likely, and I drew it. Three experience from one decision is a better rate than anything else I can do, and the kind is now known for the rest of the game. The second Yellow Potion is still an unknown kind; with Neutralize Poison out of the pool its expected value falls to about half an experience against a 15 per cent chance of Sleep, Blindness, Confusion or Poison, and Blindness would cost me the map that I am using to navigate - so the second one waits for a safe moment. (ask 176) (ask 176)
- A MONSTER IN THE CORRIDOR, AND THE STAIRCASE BELOW IT (ask 178-179): the digit string of twenty-four '6' carried me twenty-three tiles east in ONE ask - the corridor is long and straight and a digit string has no junction test - and the panel now shows a monster at (54,11), three tiles east, the glyph 'r' (a mouse or a rat), and the third down staircase at (54,20), three east and NINE SOUTH of me. So the way down is through that corridor and then south, and the mouse is standing in it. I throw oil at it rather than walk into it: the rapier's to-hit is 9 and would land on the 12 per cent floor against most depth-1 armour, while a flask hits about 73 per cent against AC 4. (ask 179) (ask 179)
- THE MOUSE DIED IN ONE FLASK (ask 179-180): 'Your Flask of oil hits the giant white mouse.' - the giant white mouse is 2 hit points and AC 4, so a flask (9 to 36 damage, 73 per cent against AC 4) finishes it every time, for 1 experience. The general rule this confirms: a depth-1 mouse is the cheapest kill in the game and a soldier ant (6 hp, AC 4, 3 experience) is the best value, while the small kobold (8 hp, AC 24, 5 experience) is the one to leave alone because oil cannot reach AC 24. (ask 180) (ask 180)
- A -more- EATS ONE KEY PER PAGE (ask 180-181): the oil message had two pages, so my first '6' was eaten by the second page and the walk ended one tile short with 'There is a wall in the way!'. Two spaces is the safe way to clear a message you cannot see the length of, and the extra spaces are harmless when there is nothing to clear. (ask 181) (ask 181)
- THE WAY DOWN AT LAST (ask 181-182): the panel showed the passage going south from the mouse's square as a one-wide corridor, and the digit string walked it straight: ten steps south put me on the down staircase, and the status line says 'Down staircase'. The third staircase of this level is at level (89,63) - the spell had known it since ask 164, and it took twenty-two decisions to walk to it from the room, of which twenty-three tiles came in ONE ask along a straight corridor and the other ten along a straight passage. What made the difference was reading the panel tile by tile instead of by eye: my printed map had a one-column offset from the true coordinates, and I twice planned a route into a wall. (ask 182) (ask 182)
- THE REST PAID BOTH THE SPELL BAR AND TWO EXPERIENCE (ask 182-183): one full rest on the down staircase filled the bar from 0/2 to 2/2 and NXT went from 3 to 1 - so the giant white mouse paid its 1 experience and something else paid 1 more, and the rest was not interrupted in this swept corridor. A rest is one decision for two spell points and about sixty game turns, which at the rate the spell points regenerate while walking (one point per 71 actions) is worth five or six decisions, and it is the only way to make spells affordable at all. The cast sequence that works: 'm' for the cast prompt, 'a' for the spell book, then '8' twice to put the menu cursor on the first row (it starts on the first row but '8' twice makes sure), then Enter to select, then a direction for the target - the menu's letters do not select, only the cursor and Enter do. (ask 183) (ask 183)
- THE SPELL MENU'S TWO RULES, MEASURED (ask 183-184): the menu's cursor starts on the SPELL I KNOW (Find Traps, row 2), a letter press only MOVES the cursor to that row and a second press of the same letter selects it (MN_DBL_TAP), and the digit keys are directions - but '8', which is up, is direction 0 and the menu's own test is 'if (dir && ...) do not', so UP DOES NOT MOVE THE CURSOR. That is why my two '8's did nothing and Enter cast Find Traps instead of Magic Missile: the message came back 'You sense the presence of stairs!' and no experience was paid, because a spell that has already worked pays nothing. The working sequence is 'm' for the prompt, the pack letter for the book, then the row letter TWICE, then a direction for the target: 'maaa6' is Magic Missile east. (ask 184) (ask 184)
- WHAT I CANNOT SEE FROM THE SCREEN (ask 184-185): the sidebar's spell point field is not always redrawn after a cast - the Find Traps cast of ask 183 showed 'SP 2/2' on the screen while the bar was really 1/2 - so I cannot trust that field immediately after a cast, and casting with too little mana is not a free error: do_cmd_cast asks 'Attempt it anyway?', and spell_cast then over-exerts the character (a fainting chance and a constitution loss). So before any cast I rest first and read the bar after the rest, where the sidebar is redrawn. (ask 185) (ask 185)
- THE MESSAGE PAGES KEEP EATING MY KEYS (ask 184-187): a Find Traps cast prints three sentences and the -more- prompt takes one key PER PAGE, and the message line even goes back to the first page, so four separate asks of 'maaa6' never reached the spell list - the cursor at (46,0) in the ask header proved that no menu was open at all. The lesson for the next session: after any message with a -more- I send several spaces in the same answer as the command I actually want, because a screen that shows a menu is not the same as a screen with a pending prompt. (ask 187) (ask 187)
- ON DEPTH 2 (ask 187-188): '> ' from the down staircase put me on depth 2 standing on its up staircase, with the level feeling 'LF:2-?' and the message 'This seems a tame, sheltered place.' The spell bar is 1/2 - the accidental Find Traps cast of ask 186 spent the point, because the -more- prompt had eaten the first two keys of my answer and the rest of the string landed on the cast prompt in the wrong order. The depth-1 level is gone now: leaving it destroyed it, so the staircase, the room, the mouse and the snake are all behind me, and the 29 asks of walking that bought me this level cannot be repeated. (ask 188) (ask 188)
- THE MENU'S CURSOR SITS ON THE SPELL I KNOW, AND THE ASK HEADER SAYS WHERE (ask 188-189): with the cast list open the header read 'cursor at 15,4', and row 4 of the screen is 'c) Find Traps, Doors & Stairs' - so the cursor starts on the learned spell, not on the first row. The spell list on this level shows Light Room at 23 per cent failure against 18 per cent on depth 1, so the failure chance moves with the character. The letter press moves the cursor and a second press of the same letter selects: 'aa' for Magic Missile, then a direction. (ask 189) (ask 189)
- THE SPELL MENU CANNOT CAST AN UNLEARNED SPELL (ask 188-190): the menu's ROWS are the filter 'spell_okay_to_cast' - the spells I have LEARNED - while the DISPLAY prints every spell in the book with 'unknown' or 'difficult' beside the ones I cannot use. So the menu has ONE row (Find Traps) and every letter selects it: my 'aa6' cast Find Traps again, and the earlier casts were all Find Traps too, not the Magic Missile I thought. The lesson: the letter is an index into the menu's rows, not into the list of letters on the screen, and a letter that names a row the menu does not have selects whatever row that index happens to be. And at CL1 I cannot STUDY anything either: the status line has no 'Study' word because my one spell slot holds Find Traps, so the +4 experience from a first Magic Missile cast is out of reach until CL2 opens a second slot. (ask 190) (ask 190)
- A DIGIT STRING CAN OPEN MENUS (ask 192-195): twelve '6' keys sent into a game that was still in a targeting prompt opened the character sheet, then the equipment list, and then the quit menu - because 'C' and Escape are commands and Escape from the character sheet is the quit command. The lesson for a mage who wants to walk: never send a long key string without knowing the game is idle, and answer 'n' at the quit prompt. (ask 195) (ask 195)

note: DECISION (ask 14): studied Find Traps, Doors & Stairs, NOT Magic Missile, contrary to my own MAGE.md 2 correction ('Magic Missile first'). Reason, mine: at CL1 the whole level-1 exp economy is the bottleneck -- CL2 needs 12 exp (Gnome 120%), the best depth-1 kill is a small kobold at 5 exp, and kobolds are AC 24, which my thrown oil (to-hit 11) can only hit on the 12% floor. Depth 2 pays double for the same kill, so one cast + one walk to the staircase it reveals moves the whole hunt to where the exp is. Magic Missile is available at CL2 (2nd slot: num_allowed = adj_mag_study x lev / 100, so CL2 allows 2), when SP also doubles (4 SP, one point per 50 actions). Evidence: class.txt mage spell list (Magic Missile L1 1sp exp 4; Find Traps L1 1sp exp 2), monster.txt (small kobold 8hp AC24 exp5 at depth1; blubbering icky thing 18hp AC4 exp8 at depth2 = 16 exp at CL1 = CL2 in one kill); hit_chance formula 12% floor. (ask 14)

note: TOWN NAVIGATION (ask 16): the aim.py recipe (* + digits + g) FAILED in the town: * opens the Target mode with the cursor on my own square, and my square was the down staircase (INTERESTING, terrain.txt flags STAIR|DOWNSTAIR|INTERESTING), so the first digit printed the description and the NEXT digit aborted the mode ('Target Aborted'), after which the rest of the string was run as raw movement and I walked 2 tiles south by accident. Source: ui-target.c target_set_interactive -> target_set_interactive_aux -> aux_terrain consumes a key whenever the cursor square is interesting, and returns true (stop) for any key that is not Enter or space. Also terrain.txt: SHOP tiles carry INTERESTING too, so aiming AT a store digit cannot work either. In the town I use plain digit walking over the drawn map instead (map.py --to gives the route); the routes it printed were checked step by step against the panel and none crosses rubble. (ask 16)

note: ARMOUR DECISION (ask 20): this Armoury has no Soft Leather Armour, no shield and no helm, so my MAGE.md shopping list does not exist in this seed; what it has is Studded Leather Armour 150 (AC12, 10 lb, to-hit -1), Robe 36 (AC2), Gauntlets 24 (AC3), Iron Shod Boots 84 (AC4), Leather Gloves 6 (AC1). I bought Studded+Robe+Gauntlets = AC 17 for 210 of 256 gold. The Studded's (-1) is a real cost and I checked it in the source: calc_bonuses (player-calcs.c) does state->to_h += obj->to_h for every worn item that is not a weapon or a bow, and chance_of_missile_hit_base (player-attack.c:134) adds p->state.to_h to the throw to-hit for a THROWING item -- and a Flask of oil carries the THROWING flag (object.txt). So the armour costs my thrown oil one point of to-hit (11 -> 10), which is ~7 points of hit rate against an AC-14 target (12+83*(11-9)/11 = 27% -> 12+83*(10-9)/10 = 20%). I judged +7 AC worth more: a depth-2 soldier with to-hit 15 hits me 12+83*(15-9)/15 = 51% of the time at AC 10 and 12+83*(15-11)/15 = 33% at AC 17. (ask 20)

note: UNKNOWN POTION, IDENTIFIED AS A POTION NOT A FLASK (ask 41): ']' says 'a Purple Speckled Potion, 7 N 1 E'. The flavour name does NOT name the kind -- lib/gamedata/flavor.txt lists 'Purple Speckled' as flavour 232, one of many random ones -- so it is an unknown kind. I recomputed the depth-1 potion pool from object.txt's alloc bands: Cure Light Wounds 80, Neutralize Poison 60, Speed 40, Heroism 40, Boldness 40, Slime Mold Juice 10, against Sleep 10, Blindness 10, Confusion 10, Poison 10, Slowness 10 -- so 270/320 good (84%) and 50/320 bad (16%). The first use pays (kind level + my level/2)/my level, so at CL1 it pays the kind's own level: expected about 1.5 experience, which is a tenth of what CL2 costs. I am CARRYING it, not drinking it: at full hit points the good outcomes (heals, heroism) mostly do nothing, while the bad tail includes Poison (object.txt: level 3, effect TIMED_INC:POISONED) and Sleep (TIMED_INC:PARALYZED), which are lethal to an 8-hit-point mage. I will drink it when I am safe, or when I need it. (ask 41)

My arithmetic says the yeek is one wake-event from waking: monster_reduce_sleep (mon-move.c) reduces a sleeping monster's sleep by 100/local_noise when the player is within about 10 tiles, and the yeek's sleep is only 10. Oil is a 12% attack against AC 16 (hit_chance: 2*AC/3 = 10 equals my to-hit 10, so I am on the flat floor), so the yeek needs about eight throws, which is about 22 damage of bites at AC 15 -- more than my 8 hit points -- and the three spiders sit next to the yeek, so hitting it wakes them (their GROUP_AI and friends:100:2d8:Same). At 8 hp and 0 spell points I was not going to open that fight. Going up costs two asks and buys a full spell bar, a safe place to try the unknown potion, and a fresh level. (ask 54)

note: THE REST PROMPT (ask 56): the field is pre-filled with '& ', so 'R' + '*' + Enter would rest only 'as needed'. The one-ask full rest is R + BACKSPACE + '*' + Enter: the first backspace deletes the whole field (src/ui-input.c 'if this is the first time round, backspace means delete all'). I am resting ON the down staircase of a fresh depth 1, so if anything comes, one '<' takes me back to the town. At 8 hit points with 0 spell points, a full bar is worth an ask. (ask 56)

note: THE TRAILING NEWLINE BYTE IS DROPPED, THE TWO-CHARACTER ESCAPE IS NOT (ask 57): I sent R + backspace + '*' + a real newline byte (printf '\n'), the field was cleared and '*' typed, but the Enter never arrived -- the screen still showed the rest prompt. The frontend drops a trailing LF byte because that is the one a text editor adds (patch/src/main-agent.c), so the Enter has to be sent as the two characters backslash-n, which the runner turns into KC_ENTER. My COMMON.md says exactly this and I still wrote it the wrong way once. (ask 57)

note: REST WORKS, AND THE SPELL BAR IS THE REAL CURRENCY (ask 58): one full rest on the down staircase took 610 game turns (61 player actions) and filled the bar from 0/2 to 2/2 -- that is 0.028 spell points an action while resting, so 71 actions for a point when awake and about 36 while resting. Resting is ONE ask, so spell points are cheap in asks and expensive in turns: what they cost is the turns you spend standing still while a level's monsters wake up. This run's whole budget should be read in that currency: a cast is worth about 70 actions of walking, and a mage's kills on depth 1 pay 1 to 5 experience each while depth 2 pays 2 to 16. (ask 58)

The lesson for me: look at the object before assuming what the glyph means -- 'l' + a direction describes the square, and the message when you pick it up names the kind. (ask 70)

note: HOW MANY MONSTERS A LEVEL HAS, AND WHERE (ask 80, from the source): classic_gen places i = z_info->level_monster_min + randint1(8) + k monsters, k = MAX(MIN(depth/3,10),2), with pick_and_place_distant_monster(c, p->grid, 0, true, depth) -- so they are placed at any distance from the up staircase (the 'distant' in the name means only 'not on the start square'), and they start ASLEEP. That is the correction to my earlier note: on a classic level the monsters are NOT kept away from the up staircase, they are simply sparse -- about fifty of them on 198x66 squares, one per 250. A corridor of ten tiles therefore holds a monster about four per cent of the time, and a 10x10 room about a third. So a room is worth ten corridors, and the Find Traps spell is worth a lot more than the staircase: it reveals the DOORS, which is a map of where the rooms are. (ask 80)

note: DECISION: THE TOWN TRIP (ask 83). What I have learned by now: exploration on a 'classic' level is slow (a run stops at every junction, so a run is 1 to 12 tiles and an aimed walk with an unknown destination gives a bogus one-tile path), the monsters are sparse (about fifty on 198x66) and they start asleep, and my spell bar is empty at 0/2 after two casts. One spell point costs about 71 actions of walking (0.014 per action), so a cast is 6 to 20 asks of running -- while the town is two '<' away and a full rest there is safe. So: go up, rest, buy a second heal and a second escape with the 55 gold, then descend with 2 spell points, one cast per level for the staircase hunt. The alternative was to keep hunting for a kill with an empty bar and 8 hit points, and that is the plan that gets a mage killed. (ask 83)

note: STAIRCASE PAIRING, MEASURED (asks 84-86): '<' (ascend) only works from an UP staircase and lands me on a DOWN staircase of the level above, and '>' (descend) only from a DOWN staircase. I walked to depth 3's up staircase, pressed '<' and arrived on depth 2's DOWN staircase; pressing '<' again did nothing at all (the turn counter did not move), which is why two '<' presses left me exactly where I was. The pairs are: town's down <-> depth 1's up, depth 1's down <-> depth 2's up, depth 2's down <-> depth 3's up. So the way UP from depth 2 is to find depth 2's UP staircase, and from there I arrive on depth 1's DOWN staircase, which needs a SECOND up staircase to reach the town. Two casts, and I have one spell point. The Scroll of Word of Recall in my pack is the cheap way: read it in the dungeon and it takes me to the town, for the price of its 15 to 34 player-turn timer. (ask 86)

note: THE AIMED AND LOOK-MODE WALKS ARE SHORT WHEN THE GROUND BETWEEN IS UNKNOWN (ask 116): 'l>g' moved one tile and stopped, although the staircase the spell found is known. The reason is in find_path (player-path.c): only_known = square_isknown(start) AND square_isknown(dest), so with a known destination but unknown ground in between the path is computed over remembered ground only and comes out short or empty. The M map knows where the staircase is (two of them, at box 9,7 and box 26,4, against my box 13,12) but the panel does not show it, so the route has to be walked in pieces. The look-mode trick is the piece that works: a direction key in look mode jumps the cursor to the NEXT INTERESTING SQUARE and the message line names it with its exact offset, which is also how I learn how far the staircase is. (ask 116)

note: THE WALK IS SHORT BECAUSE THE GROUND BETWEEN IS NOT KNOWN (ask 117): on a fresh level only the square I stand on, the squares the detection spell memorised (the doors and the stairs) and the few tiles my torch lights are known. find_path's only_known test needs BOTH ends known and a path over remembered ground, and there is none between me and a staircase 15 tiles north, so the walk is one tile. The piece that works is plain digit walking: a digit string stops only at a WALL, not at a turn, so eight '8's in one ask cover eight tiles of corridor if the corridor runs straight, and the message line says how far it got. note: THE MONSTER DENSITY, MEASURED (asks 116-122): the level has z_info->level_monster_min + randint1(8) + k monsters, about fifty, on 13,068 squares -- one per 250. My torch shows a 3x3 patch, so to sweep the level I would have to walk about 260 squares, and my best walking rate is about eight tiles an ask, so a search for one kill is thirty asks. That is the real bottleneck of this run, and it is not the fighting: the fighting is cheap (a flask of oil is 9 to 36 damage and a giant green frog on depth 2 dies to one or two), the FINDING is expensive. The Find Traps spell is worth more for its doors than for its stairs, because a door is a map of where the rooms are, and a room is a hundred squares of concentrated search. (ask 122)

note: WHY THE RUN COMMAND IS USELESS IN THE DARK (ask 153-154, from the source): run_test (player-path.c) stops the run when the ground ahead is not a known corridor - it looks at the three squares around the new direction and if a KNOWN square there is 'interesting' or if the run would have to choose between three unknown directions, it stops. So a run walks to the EDGE OF THE KNOWN MAP and no further: mine stopped after one tile at (34,13) because (33,14),(34,14),(35,14) are unknown. The AIMED WALK ('*' then digits then 'g') is the tool for the dark, because find_path treats unknown ground as passable there. And a plain digit string is immune to all of this: it walks until a wall and drops the rest. (ask 154) (ask 154)

note: THE FIRST-CAST EXPERIENCE, FROM THE SOURCE (ask 161): player-spell.c line 527-533 pays 'e * spell->slevel' the first time a spell WORKS, where e is the last field of the class.txt spell line: Find Traps 2 x 1 = 2, Light Room 4 x 1 = 4, Magic Missile 4 x 1 = 4. So a first cast of Light Room is worth 4 experience - a third of the 12 a Gnome needs for CL2 - and it also lights every square within two grids and, because I am in a room, the WHOLE ROOM, which shows me every monster standing in it. Two costs I did not know: the mana is taken whether the cast succeeds or fails (the smana block is outside the success branch), and a failure signals EVENT_INPUT_FLUSH, which is the input flush that eats the rest of a key string. Also measured: the throw sequence is Escape (to clear the monster list's 'press any key'), 'v' (throw prompt), 'a' (the flask of oil - the throw list has its own letters and oil is 'a'), '4' (that direction) - and it worked in one ask: 'Your Flask of oil hits the white worm mass.' (ask 161) (ask 161)

note: HOW THE CAST MENU REALLY WORKS (ask 163-165): the spell list is a scroll menu. Its letters do not select - pressing 'b' for Light Room only MOVED the cursor to that row and left the menu open (the menu wants a double tap), and the trailing space does nothing because all seven rows fit on one page. The digit keys are directions, so '2' moved the cursor down one row and Enter selected the row under it - which is how I cast Find Traps by accident: the cursor had been on Light Room (row 1) and my '2' took it to row 2, Find Traps. A NEW menu starts with the cursor on row 0, so Enter alone selects Magic Missile. The rule for this game: MOVE the cursor with a digit, then press Enter - never trust the letter. The cast printed 'You sense no traps. You sense no doors.' which is the third effect of a Find Traps cast (the doors were already known), and the message ends in -more-, so the next answer starts with a space. (ask 165) (ask 165)

note: THE SPELL MENU'S TWO RULES, MEASURED (ask 183-184): the menu's cursor starts on the SPELL I KNOW (Find Traps, row 2), a letter press only MOVES the cursor to that row and a second press of the same letter selects it (MN_DBL_TAP), and the digit keys are directions - but '8', which is up, is direction 0 and the menu's own test is 'if (dir && ...) do not', so UP DOES NOT MOVE THE CURSOR. That is why my two '8's did nothing and Enter cast Find Traps instead of Magic Missile: the message came back 'You sense the presence of stairs!' and no experience was paid, because a spell that has already worked pays nothing. The working sequence is 'm' for the prompt, the pack letter for the book, then the row letter TWICE, then a direction for the target: 'maaa6' is Magic Missile east. (ask 184) (ask 184)

note: WHAT I CANNOT SEE FROM THE SCREEN (ask 184-185): the sidebar's spell point field is not always redrawn after a cast - the Find Traps cast of ask 183 showed 'SP 2/2' on the screen while the bar was really 1/2 - so I cannot trust that field immediately after a cast, and casting with too little mana is not a free error: do_cmd_cast asks 'Attempt it anyway?', and spell_cast then over-exerts the character (a fainting chance and a constitution loss). So before any cast I rest first and read the bar after the rest, where the sidebar is redrawn. (ask 185) (ask 185)

note: THE SPELL MENU CANNOT CAST AN UNLEARNED SPELL (ask 188-190): the menu's ROWS are the filter 'spell_okay_to_cast' - the spells I have LEARNED - while the DISPLAY prints every spell in the book with 'unknown' or 'difficult' beside the ones I cannot use. So the menu has ONE row (Find Traps) and every letter selects it: my 'aa6' cast Find Traps again, and the earlier casts were all Find Traps too, not the Magic Missile I thought. The lesson: the letter is an index into the menu's rows, not into the list of letters on the screen, and a letter that names a row the menu does not have selects whatever row that index happens to be. And at CL1 I cannot STUDY anything either: the status line has no 'Study' word because my one spell slot holds Find Traps, so the +4 experience from a first Magic Missile cast is out of reach until CL2 opens a second slot. (ask 190) (ask 190)

note: A DIGIT STRING CAN OPEN MENUS (ask 192-195): twelve '6' keys sent into a game that was still in a targeting prompt opened the character sheet, then the equipment list, and then the quit menu - because 'C' and Escape are commands and Escape from the character sheet is the quit command. The lesson for a mage who wants to walk: never send a long key string without knowing the game is idle, and answer 'n' at the quit prompt. (ask 195) (ask 195)
